correctness.rationale: The group algebra equals the squarefree 32-dimensional algebra in characteristic two. Explicit automorphism normal forms classify all nonzero quadratic leading terms; for decomposable quadratics the residual cubic volume coefficient gives rank eight or ten via tensor-product squarezero block ranks. Dual alternating forms classify the cubic leading term, and every other leading degree is handled directly. Gaussian counts and coefficient exponents follow from disjoint fibers. The original multiplication matrices have been checked exhaustively for canonical binary perturbations and sampled over F4. Limitation: experiments are not the proof and do not exhaust every algebra element.

originality.rationale: Comparison by actual mathematical implication against accessible exterior-ideal and modular group-algebra literature found partial prior coverage of linear-part freeness and homogeneous generic principal ideals, but not a theorem giving the characteristic-two elementwise five-generator rank polynomial and first inhomogeneous cubic obstruction. No close published research record was found in scientific searches. The comparison is best-knowledge and not independent global priority certification.
residual_risks: No exhaustive historical priority certification: an unlocated group-algebra Jordan-type enumeration or a general exterior-ideal stratification could imply the theorem.

value.rationale: The problem concerns the natural principal-ideal size/Jordan rank invariant of the regular module of an elementary abelian 2-group. Five generators mark the first genuinely inhomogeneous obstruction: identical leading quadratic forms can have principal-ideal dimensions eight and ten. The rank support and exact q-dependent distribution across all labeled elements supply a complete finite-field benchmark with conceptual normal forms and sharp boundary, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
